newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Businessman Koo to represent Taiwan at APEC - Manila.
newsitem.headline: Businessman Koo to represent Taiwan at APEC - Manila.

text.p: Prominent businessman Koo Chen-Fu has been designated as Taiwan's representative to the APEC leaders' summit on November 25, the Philippines said on Monday.

"As the APEC chair this year, the Philippines received Chinese Taipei's advice of the designation of Mr. Koo Chen-Fu as its representative to the APEC Economic Leaders Meeting in Subic," the foreign affairs department said in a statement.
Koo also represented Taiwan at last year's APEC summit in Osaka, Japan.
Koo is the chairman of Taiwan Cement Corp, the honorary chairman of China Trust Commercial Bank and the founder of the Taiwan Institute for Economic Research.

Diplomatic sources said Taiwan tried to upgrade its participation in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum summit by submitting the name of vice president Lien Chan last month, but the Philippine government rejected the bid.

China had said it would not accept any plans to upgrade the representation of rival Taiwan at the meeting. China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war separated them in 1949 and has decried any attempts by the island to win broader international recognition.

The summit is expected to bring together leaders from Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Singapore, Thailand, Taiwan and the United States.
